::: {#exr-mouse-build-tv}
Recall that same() and flat() have very simple algebraic definitions:

$\text{steady}(x) \equiv x\ \ \ \ \text{and}\ \ \ \ \ \text{flat}( ) \equiv 1$

Flat() is so simple that it does not even require an arg! The simplicity means that we can write @eq-lc-fghz in a more compact form: 

$$h(x, z) \equiv a\, x + b\, z + c .$$ {#eq-lc-fghz2}

The conciseness of @eq-lc-fghz2, unfortunately, hides something important: same() and flat() are a modeler's choice, usually just an approximation. When this choice is not appropriate, remember that a modeler can use other functions instead of same().
:::
 <!-- end of exr-mouse-build-tv -->
